headline: Revenue grows on USDC scale, but costs squeeze GAAP profit
summary_short: Circle's Q1 2026 revenue rose 20% y/y to $694.1M as USDC in circulation grew 28% to $77.0B, but GAAP net income fell 14.7% to $55.3M on higher stock-based compensation and distribution costs, even as management's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $151M.
summary_long: Reserve income (94% of revenue) rose $94.6M as a 39.1% rise in average USDC in circulation outweighed a 66bp yield decline from Fed rate cuts; other revenue nearly doubled on integration, blockchain-rewards and fund-management fees. Distribution and transaction costs rose 16.7% to $405.4M, chiefly higher Coinbase and Binance payments. Operating expenses rose on compensation (+82.7%, RSU vesting tied to the 2025 IPO), G&A (+86.6%, legal fees and a Circle Foundation stock contribution) and D&A (+92.8%, software amortization), pushing operating income down 51.6% to $45.0M. Net income fell 14.7% to $55.3M as a lower 2.5% effective tax rate and $11.7M other income partly offset the decline. No forward guidance was given. Cash fell 1.7% q/q to $1,517.3M.

drivers.explanation: Reserve income (94% of revenue) rose $94.6M as a 39.1% rise in average USDC in circulation outweighed a 66bp decline in average yields from Fed rate actions; other revenue nearly doubled on integration services, blockchain rewards, redemption fees and fund management.

Distribution and transaction costs rose 16.7% to $405.4M, driven by a $27.4M rise in Coinbase distribution payments (higher reserve income and on-platform balances) plus $30.6M combined growth in Binance and other partner distribution costs.

This shard-level EBITDA uses a generic operating-income-plus-D&A definition; it fell on the same cost pressures below. It differs from Circle's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which rose 24% to $151M after excluding stock-based comp and other items.
Tracks the operating-income decline: revenue growth was outpaced by compensation (+82.7%), G&A (+86.6%) and D&A (+92.8%) expense growth, per the release's expense-line discussion.

Compensation expense rose 82.7% on stock-based comp tied to RSU vesting triggered by the 2025 IPO and higher headcount; G&A rose 86.6% on legal/professional fees and a Circle Foundation stock contribution; D&A rose 92.8% on software amortization.

The operating-income decline was partly offset by other income swinging to +$11.7M (interest income, FX gains, investment gains) from -$3.1M, and a lower 2.5% effective tax rate (vs 27.9%) on stock-comp tax benefits.
Pretax income fell as the operating-income decline outweighed the swing to positive other income of $11.7M from a $3.1M expense a year earlier.

Sequential decline from $0.56 tracks the net-income drop from Q4 2025 plus a rise in basic weighted shares; the y/y comparison isn't meaningful since Q1 2025 EPS rounded to $0.00 under the pre-IPO preferred-stock structure.

Sequential decline from $0.43 tracks lower net income plus higher diluted weighted shares (266.7M vs 75.65M a year earlier, reflecting the June 2025 IPO preferred-to-common conversion and August 2025 follow-on offering).

The cash-flow statement's largest reconciling swing was accounts payable and accrued expenses moving to -$101.4M from +$6.4M a year earlier; the release's MD&A does not narrate a specific cause for this working-capital swing.
Per the MD&A's investing-activities breakdown, purchases of long-lived assets rose to $9.4M from $5.9M, alongside $15.6M of capitalized software development costs (up from $11.7M).

The release does not attribute this specific y/y balance change to a stated cause in this quarter's MD&A (which discusses only the q/q -1.7% sequential move); not explained in the release for the y/y comparison.

The y/y jump reflects the June 2025 IPO, which converted all outstanding preferred stock ($1.1B carrying value) into common equity and added $583.0M of net IPO proceeds, plus $444.8M of net proceeds from the August 2025 follow-on offering, both disclosed in Note 1.
Share count expansion reflects the June 2025 IPO's preferred-to-common conversion (139.8M shares) and new shares issued in the IPO and August 2025 follow-on offering, both disclosed in Note 1.

Platform growth (USDC in circulation +28% to $77.0B, onchain volume +263% to $21.5T) drove revenue and non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA higher, but GAAP profit compressed as IPO-triggered stock compensation, distribution costs and D&A grew faster than revenue.
